messages:
josh: Quick signal — ruby sampleapp streaming demo gets weird stalls on macOS when we open multiple streaming connections. Root cause looks like Net::HTTP not doing HTTP/2 multiplexing, so concurrent streams serialize. I opened a small PR switching the client adapter to httpx for streaming paths: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ruby-sdk/pull/3456

sam: Saw the PR, thanks for the writeup. A couple quick concerns: httpx adds extra deps and historically some adapters pull in native extensions that cause CI matrix pain. Is httpx pure-ruby on all our supported platforms?

nora: FWIW I reproduced locally on an M1 Mac — with Net::HTTP two concurrent streams block and the second stream waits for the first to finish headers. Switching to httpx locally fixed the concurrency (much lower tail latency). Numbers: 350ms -> ~70ms median on a 4-stream loop.

ci-bot: GitHub Actions: ruby-ci (PR #3456) — workflow failed on ubuntu-20.04 matrix: "Too many open files" during integration_test_streaming.rb:line 42. Full log: https://ci.example.com/builds/99876

eva: Quick context: our hosted edge/proxy supports multiplexing and we don't terminate streams into separate TCP connections, so client-side multiplexing really matters for demos and local perf. I like an adapter approach so we can keep Net::HTTP as default for compatibility but opt into httpx for improved streaming. Can we make it pluggable via env var and document it in sampleapp?

sam: Agreed on pluggable adapter. Two suggestions for the PR: 1) keep httpx optional under a new gem group in the gemspec so folks on windows/air-gapped envs don't get surprises, 2) add a short integration test that asserts two concurrent streaming responses make progress (to catch regressions).

josh: Updated PR: added adapter selector REDWOOD_HTTP_ADAPTER (values: nethttp|httpx), moved httpx to :streaming group in the gemspec, and added a simple concurrency smoke test. Gemfile snippet: ```ruby
# Gemfile
group :streaming do
  gem 'httpx'
end
```
And usage: ```ruby
adapter = ENV.fetch('REDWOOD_HTTP_ADAPTER','nethttp')
client = Redwood::Client.new(adapter: adapter)
```

nora: Ran the updated branch CI locally and re-ran the failing test with ulimit bumped — integration test passes now, and the earlier "too many open files" was a flaky env issue on GH runners. Streaming perf on mac looks great. :rocket:

sam: Thanks, Josh. I left a few small comments (changelog entry, mention adapter env var in sampleapp README, and an extra spec edge-case for when httpx isn't available). Once addressed I can approve. :+1:

ci-bot: GitHub Actions: ruby-ci (PR #3456) — all checks passed on branch 'httpx-adapter' (ubuntu-22.04 / macos-latest / windows-latest).

josh: Awesome — will push the README + changelog tweaks this afternoon and request merge. Can someone from devex to cut a 0.8.x release after merge?

eva: Will coordinate release. Also let's add a short note in the console docs about adapter selection for developers who hit streaming edge cases.

sam: Sounds good. Thanks everyone for the quick reviews and the perf datapoints.
